_comment: Canned answers so the harness, the demo page and CI run with no model at all. The fixture client picks a reading by the app the prompt is about, so the demo stays coherent without inventing a model. These are plausible, not clever: they exist so a broken install still shows the shape of the thing instead of an error.

intent.situation: Your mum is asking whether you are coming on Sunday. Your aunt needs a number for lunch, and a deadline is already in the thread - Friday.
intent.what_they_want: A yes or a no, and how many people. Not a maybe.
intent.what_you_want: Not to commit until you know, without making her chase you a third time.
open_questions: Are you actually free on Sunday?
noticed: The deadline is your mum's promise to your aunt, not your own
Three separate questions arrived in one go - only the last one is a question

options.text: yeah i'll be there, just me
options.why: Answers both questions in six words.

options.text: i'm in unless something blows up at work - can i confirm thursday?
options.why: Gives her a real date to tell your aunt instead of leaving her to chase.

options.text: can't do this sunday, sorry - tell her i'll come the week after
options.why: Says no once, and offers the next one so it is not a dead end.

suggested_intents: just say yes to family things
ask for a day to decide without apologising for it

intent.situation: The channel is arranging Saturday. Jules needs a number tonight to book, and Bram has already made a joke about you being asleep.
intent.what_they_want: A yes or no from you so the table can be booked.
intent.what_you_want: To answer without it becoming a whole thing in front of everyone.
open_questions: Do you actually want to go on Saturday?
noticed: This is a server: six other people can read whatever you send
Jules set a deadline of tonight, which is two words long and easy to miss

options.why: Closes the loop in five words, which is what the channel is for.

options.text: yep count me in - what time?
options.why: Says yes and gets the one detail that is actually missing.

options.text: probably, let me check something and i'll confirm tonight
options.why: Keeps the door open honestly, and repeats the deadline back.

suggested_intents: answer in servers briefly, not with a paragraph

intent.situation: Priya is asking you to own a production migration cutover on the 14th, while she is away. She wants a name in the doc today. You have already said you would check your calendar.
intent.what_they_want: A yes or no today so she can plan around it.
intent.what_you_want: To be helpful without quietly agreeing to be on call for a week you have not looked at.
open_questions: Who covers it if the rollback runs past midnight?
noticed: 'Mostly watching dashboards' is her estimate, not a commitment
She is away that week: if it goes wrong, you are the only name in the doc
This is a work channel - the doc and her manager may both quote your reply

options.text: i can own the cutover itself on the 14th, but i'll need someone on the rollback path while you're out - can we name that today?
options.why: Says yes to the part you can do and makes the missing cover visible before it is your problem.

options.text: let me look at the 14th properly after standup and i'll confirm by 11
options.why: Honours the deadline she set without agreeing to anything blind.

options.text: i can't take the cutover that week, but i can do the dashboard watch on the 15th
options.why: A clean no with a real offer attached, which reads better than a slow yes.

suggested_intents: never agree to on-call cover in the first message
answer with what i can do, not what i might

intent.situation: Sam apologised last night after an argument. You have since sent three messages and there has been no reply - the last one asks whether you are okay.
intent.what_they_want: Space, probably. Nothing in the thread says otherwise.
intent.what_you_want: Reassurance, which is why the messages keep coming.
open_questions: Is Sam asleep, at work, or avoiding you?
How much of this do you want to have said tomorrow?
noticed: Three messages in a row, the last of which was sent at 22:48
You have already apologised once for the same thing tonight
The thread reads like a search for reassurance, not for a reply

options.text: no rush, i'm around tomorrow if you want to talk
options.why: Ends the run of messages without asking for anything back.

options.text: going to sleep - we'll sort it out, i'm not going anywhere
options.why: A last line that settles the thing instead of reopening it.

options.text: i'll leave you to it. message me when you're ready
options.why: Puts the next move in their hands, which is where it belongs tonight.

intent.situation: Dana, who you met once at a meetup, is hiring a staff engineer and wants a call this week. She has already softened the ask so a no is cheap.
intent.what_they_want: A yes, a no, or a date for a short call.
intent.what_you_want: To keep the door open without pretending to be more interested than you are.
noticed: You met once, briefly - do not write as if you know her
She has given you an easy exit, so a slow no costs you nothing
Every sentence here could be forwarded to a hiring panel

options.text: Thanks for reaching out - I'm not looking to move right now, but I'd be glad to stay in touch.
options.why: A clean no that keeps the relationship, and nothing to walk back later.

options.text: Happy to talk. I'm free Thursday after 4pm or Friday morning - would either work?
options.why: Turns the ask into a concrete slot, which is what she asked for.

options.text: Flattered, but I'm not the right fit for a runtime team. If you're hiring on inference infra, that's closer to my work.
options.why: Declines the role and points at the one you would want.

suggested_intents: decline recruiter messages in one sentence
never claim to remember a meeting i don't

intent.situation: Someone sent a message and you have not answered yet.
intent.what_they_want: An answer, or at least an acknowledgement.
noticed: No profile for this app, so the norms are unknown

options.text: yeah, sorry, been flat out. what's the ask?
options.why: Opens the door without promising anything.

options.text: give me a bit and i'll come back to this properly
options.why: Buys time honestly instead of going quiet.

sms.why: This is another apology into a thread that has already had several, and it promises something about tonight you cannot keep.
sms.fix: i'm sorry, i know i keep saying it. no pressure to reply tonight.
sms.alt: no pressure to reply tonight. i'm around tomorrow if you want to talk.

slack.why: This says yes to the whole week, including the part Priya is being careful not to promise.
slack.fix: I can own the cutover on the 14th — who's covering the rollback path while you're out?
slack.alt: I can own the cutover itself, but I'll need a named cover for the rollback path. Can we sort that today?

linkedin.why: It implies a shared history you do not have and commits you further than you meant.

generic.why: Something in this would be hard to walk back once it is sent.
